author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: In the Forcepoint Security Manager, set the syslog server under Settings > General > Remediation, add Audit Incident > Send Syslog Message to the action plans whose incidents you want, and, on 10.2 or later, tick Send syslog message under Logs > Audit log. Incidents and incident risk ranking cases (header name DLP Syslog) go to the third-party alert schema: the event ID, policy categories as the title, action, channel and details as the summary, severityType as severity, blocked for Blocked, Quarantined, dropped and Denied actions, the login name, source address and host, the URL for web channels, and the source, destinations, attachments, sensor and match count in additional_data. Risk ranking cases add the risk score and the incident IDs. Audit log messages go to Management Event with the administrator, topic and change. System log messages stay generic. Forcepoint doesn't document the scale of the header severity, so it is kept as vendor_severity unless severityType (the Audit Quality fields) is there. timeStamp has no time zone and is read as UTC. Forcepoint's published template has no space before analyzedBy= and sourceIp=; the samples assume normal CEF spacing. Before 8.4 the header reads Websense or Forcepoint with TRITON AP-DATA, which also matches. Samples are made up in the documented templates. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (78 of 78 fields matched the emulator), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there. Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (76 of 76 fields). No built-in parser, including the Forcepoint NGFW and Web Security ones, claimed these lines in 12 Run Tests.
